summary: This work demonstrates a parametrically driven iSWAP gate between fixed-frequency transmons coupled via a capacitively shunted double-transmon coupler (CSDTC), achieving 99.92(2)% fidelity with 112 ns total duration at zero flux bias. The gate uses second-harmonic activation of the exchange interaction through a sinusoidal flux drive, avoiding large flux excursions and predistortion calibration required by baseband-flux CZ gates on the same device.
motivation: Baseband flux-controlled two-qubit gates require large flux amplitudes vulnerable to pulse distortion and qubit-coupler hybridization, while parametric gates typically need flux bias away from the zero-flux sweet spot. A scheme combining zero-flux-bias operation with parametric activation could reduce both flux noise sensitivity and control complexity.
method: A sinusoidal flux drive at frequency $\omega_d \approx \Delta_{21}/2$ modulates the CSDTC M-mode frequency at $2\omega_d$, parametrically activating iSWAP interaction via second-order energy-level modulation. The implementation uses a simple tanh-shaped envelope [Eq. (25)] with fixed $\beta/2\pi = 290$ MHz, requiring only frame-update calibration without waveform predistortion.
result: At optimal duration $t_\mathrm{tot} = 112$ ns including 12 ns idling, the gate achieves $r_\mathrm{iSWAP}^D = 0.078(15)\%$ depolarization error and $L_1 = 0.011(7)\%$ leakage, yielding total infidelity $\epsilon = 0.08(2)\%$. The effective coherence time $T_D^{\mathrm{iSWAP}} = 57(11)$ μs exceeds prior DTC/CSDTC CZ implementations due to reduced coupler hybridization ($\bar{p}_c \approx 0.05$ vs. 0.40) and dynamical ZZ suppression ($\zeta_\mathrm{eff}/2\pi = -4.7$ kHz at optimal amplitude).
